title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: oriented topological surfaces X, Y of finite type (compact minus finitely many points). Page 1 defined Hom_isot(X,Y) as the set of path-components of the space of finite étale maps (finite coverings) X→Y, i.e. maps modulo isotopy. An isotopy is a map F: X×I→Y×I over I. Pull back along the homotopy equivalence Y→Y×I: since Y'↦Y'×I is an equivalence of finite étale covers, F identifies X×I with Y'×I over Y×I, for a finite étale cover p: Y'→Y.

This page draws the consequence. f and g are isotopic iff there is a finite étale cover p: Y'→Y and homeomorphisms f0, g0: X ≅ Y' with f = p f0, g = p g0, and f0, g0 isotopic. Equivalently g0 = f0∘u with u: X≅X isotopic to the identity. Then g = p f0 u = f∘u.

Proposition 1: two finite étale maps (Grothendieck writes 'immersions') f, g: X→Y are isotopic iff g = f∘u for some automorphism u of X isotopic to id. So the isotopy class of f is the orbit of f under the identity component Homeo_0(X) acting by precomposition.

The page ends by starting to analyse an isotopy class of f in the isotopic category. The next page passes to automorphisms of finite order of Y'. Its Proposition 2: for anabelian surfaces (χ<0), a finite-order automorphism isotopic to the identity is the identity, even if it only acts trivially on H_1 with Z/n coefficients, n≥3 (Serre's lemma). This is the setting for defining the 'Teichmüller/isotopic' category of surfaces on which Gal(Q̄/Q) is to act.
errors: Minor imprecision: what is unique up to unique isomorphism is the pair (Y', identification α), i.e. Y' as a cover together with f0. Y' alone has nontrivial deck automorphisms, so it is not unique up to unique isomorphism.

The converse direction (g = f u with u isotopic to id implies f isotopic to g) is immediate. The forward direction tacitly uses that the I-family α is fibrewise a homeomorphism; this is fine since α commutes with the projections to I. Orientation conditions were crossed out on page 1, so it is unclear whether u must preserve orientation (automatic if u is isotopic to id). No real error.

ideas.what: Isotopy classes of finite étale maps of surfaces equal orbits under precomposition by homeomorphisms isotopic to identity (via lifting the isotopy to a cover Y')
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy invariance of finite covers; Hom in the isotopy (mapping-class) category of surfaces with finite covering maps
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore (covering space theory); the isotopic/Teichmüller category of surfaces is associated with Grothendieck's Esquisse and later Teichmüller-tower work (Lochak, Schneps, Nakamura, etc.)
ideas.where_published: The Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and mapping class groupoids, but not this elementary lemma explicitly as far as I know

ideas.what: Category whose objects are finite-type oriented surfaces and whose morphisms are isotopy classes of finite étale maps
ideas.modern_name: Isotopy category of surfaces / topological model of the category of hyperbolic curves with étale maps (anabelian setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, Lettre à Faltings), later formalized by others
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), letter to Faltings (1983) in spirit

deep.surprise_reason: The page proves an elementary covering-space lemma setting up the isotopic category of surfaces. It is correct and routine. It is foundational to the Teichmüller/anabelian program but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'revêt{+ram.+}/étale' : the insertion above 'rev.' likely reads 'fini', i.e. 'un revêtement fini étale'. 'ram.' (ramifié) contradicts the context.
'soient congrues' should probably read 'soient congrus' (referring to f, g); in the manuscript, 'qu'ils' is used.
Line '(9) u : X ≃ X est est un homéom.' : the duplicated 'est' is a transcription artifact; read 'u : X ≃ X est un homéomorphisme de X sur lui-même isotope à l'identité'.
